prompt:
Create a complete 1440 × 900 desktop web portfolio homepage for John Paul Fernandez, edge to edge without a browser frame. The audience is potential clients and collaborators looking for his real profile, technical range, and product-building approach. Use the supplied real portrait reference and preserve John’s identity.

This is composition option two within The Cutaway Folio, not a new visual direction. Keep its cobalt, coral-red, acid-yellow, chalk, and graphite cutaway language, architectural section marks, and bold editorial typography with compact labels. Let one continuous cutaway band run horizontally across the page in three connected zones: Interfaces, Applications, Backend systems. Build a large cobalt profile field above it, with name and portrait sharing the same structure; carry the exact profile paragraph and “See my work” action into the field. Keep the entire diagram readable and visually connected, then let the Selected projects section begin below as a quiet chalk plane. Make the silhouette and flow clearly different from the original composition; no cards, no dashboard, no split hero, no new art direction.

Use exactly: “John Paul Fernandez”, “Full Stack Developer”, “Fast, clear, dependable web products”, “I like building web products that feel fast, clear, and dependable. Most of my work lives at the intersection of React interfaces, Next.js apps, and backend systems that are simple to scale and maintain.”, “3+ years building web products”, “Interfaces”, “Applications”, “Backend systems”. Include only React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Docker, Git, Firebase, and Nginx. Navigation is About, Work, Experience, Contact. Start the next section with “Selected projects” and “Project writeups are not published yet”. Do not invent other copy, projects, metrics, clients, employers, or testimonials.
